title: Agent runtime client app slice: the sources leave the login name, the run-step path, the added fallback event, the client flag and the route path open
source: RWB-TE-013 legacy story sections 3, 5, 12 and 13; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1 and T3.1; Arch v5 slides 16 and 41; RWB-P10-TE013-CON placeholder set
description: The legacy story names an in-process interface and no REST operation, so the run-step path below the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 is not in any source; it names a decision log entry and no statement of which library event carries a step fallback that produced no agent run; it names a feature flag rwb.agent.client without naming the flag store of the target; it names the admin read on the legacy monolith base without the gateway-bff route in front of it; and no source names the login of the service. Each element is named and fixed by assumption, not by invention of a business value.
evidence: Legacy section 12 declares AgentStepClient.runStep as a Java interface and GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-runs only; Arch v5 slide 43 catalogues AgentRunCompleted alone on rwb.agent.events.v1; TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 lists no run-step operation.
area: P10 rwb-agent agent runtime client (APP slice)
proposed: Fix the run-step path in RWB-P10-TE013-CON and reuse it here; keep AgentStepFallback on rwb.agent.events.v1; keep rwb.agent.client as a platform flag row; take the route from the edge story; name the login from the P10 DB story and reference it as a secret.

title: Agent runtime client contract slice: the run-step path, the added fallback event, the REST member detail, the error taxonomy, the record lookup and the route path are not specified
source: RWB-TE-013 legacy story sections 12 and 14; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1, T-A.2 and T3.2; Arch v5 slides 16 and 43; RWB-P10-E1058-CON baseline
description: The contract fixes the operation, the shapes, the reason vocabulary, the record mapping, the two event payloads and the fakes, but no source names the path below the base, the media type and member detail of the REST request and answer, the business code per refusal, the record lookup form of the local library, or the gateway-bff route name and path. Every one of these is fixed by an assumption that is visible in the document and testable against the fakes.
evidence: Legacy section 12 gives Java records and an interface and no HTTP method or path; TSD P10 v2 T-A.2 lists the platform operations only; Arch v5 slide 20 names the gateway-bff route as a composite and no path.
area: P10 rwb-agent agent runtime client (CON slice)
proposed: Publish the operation and the mapping in the contract, keep the legacy reason wording, and let the edge story own the route path once it is agreed.

title: Agent runtime client deployment slice: the login name, the fallback sweep Schedule, the consumer group, the route path, the topology and the model endpoint detail are not specified
source: RWB-TE-013 legacy story sections 3, 12 and 13; Arch v5 slides 16, 20, 41 and 44; RWB-P10-TE013-CON; RWB-P10-E1058-CON
description: The deployment needs a Schedule name and cadence for the sweep that replaces the legacy Quartz and job entry, a consumer group for the reconciliation read, the login reference, the gateway-bff route path, the topology values and the host, port and certificate of the model endpoint. No source names any of them, so each is a value of the environment or of another story and is fixed here by assumption and by reference.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 retires the shared Quartz tables and names no Schedule for this key; slide 41 names the queue rwb-agent and no group; TSD P10 v2 T5.1 names INT-23 without a host or a port.
area: P10 rwb-agent agent runtime client (OPS slice)
proposed: Register the sweep as a Schedule in namespace rwb-recovery on the queue rwb-agent, name the group of the sweep, and take the endpoint and topology detail from the infrastructure story and the values files.
